entities.summary: Thomas Lumley-Saunderson, 3rd Earl of Scarbrough, KB was a British peer, British Army officer and diplomat. Born in unknown, he served as a Member of Parliament for Scarbrough from 1729 to 1734 and as a British Army officer during the War of the Austrian Succession. Lumley-Saunderson was a key figure in the development of the British East India Company's military presence in India. He was a prominent diplomat and played a role in the Anglo-French Treaty of 1743. The Earl of Scarbrough's legacy can be seen in the continued growth of British trade and military influence in Asia during the 18th century. Lumley-Saunderson's diplomatic efforts helped secure a significant trade agreement with China, leading to increased British exports of textiles and other goods. The Earl's military service also contributed to the expansion of British territory in India, shaping the country's future political landscape. His contributions to British diplomacy and trade had a lasting impact on the country's relations with Asian nations. The Earl of Scarbrough's story serves as a testament to the complex and multifaceted nature of British colonial expansion during the 18th century. Lumley-Saunderson's experiences in India and his role in shaping British diplomacy and trade had a profound effect on the country's future, making him a significant figure in the arc of world history.
